originalTitle: Adam Ramsay-Peaty armed with ‘battle plan’ for golden revival in 50m breaststroke
summary: The Briton is ready to bounce back after his 100m breaststroke bronze at the Commonwealth Games and he said: ‘The last 24 hours have been a bit of a whirlwind’
content: Adam Ramsay-Peaty has never been one to hide his emotions. He wears them proudly on his sleeve, next to the striking tattoos of a huge lion and Poseidon, the Greek god of the sea. After his shock defeat in the 100m breaststroke final at these Commonwealth Games, the 31-year-old was back pouring his heart out on Sunday – and insisting he had a “battle plan” to win gold in Monday’s 50m breaststroke final. Ramsay-Peaty certainly looked smoother in qualifying third fastest from the semi-finals in 26.82sec. However, he still has a couple of tenths to find on the South African Michael Houlie, who was fastest in 26.61. The Australian Sam Williamson, who is hoping to add the 50m to his 100m crown, also looked good as he won his semi-final in 26.79. Yet Peaty pronounced himself happy with how he had bounced back from Saturday’s shock loss. “It felt much better,” he said. “The last 24 hours have been a bit of a whirlwind, but I’m really happy with that. We’re on a great trajectory for tomorrow. “For me, the best way to ever get anything out of my head is just to write it out. When I write down what’s going wrong, what’s going right, what kind of change? What can’t change? Then I’ve got a battle plan.” He added: “People forget that I haven’t done this for two years. And even I forget that. So as you go through heats, semis and finals, it’s quite difficult if you’re not used to it. So I think that perspective is a good thing.” Peaty has stood on the top of the podium 32 times in global championships across his glittering career. Yet he has not won a gold medal since the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games. That record was extended on Saturday when he could take only bronze in the 100m breaststroke in 59.65, behind Williamson, who won in 59.3, and the brilliant 18-year-old Filip Nowicki from Jersey. Afterwards Ramsay-Peaty was strikingly honest about “all the shit I have been through” to get ready for the Commonwealth Games, including the 5.30am starts, missing family gatherings because of training, and also the amount of abuse he and his family has received on social media. On Sunday he added more context to his struggles, pointing out that he battled with burnout and a broken foot over the past four years, as well as hinting at the much-publicised estrangement with his family. “There have been a multitude of things at play over the last few years – burnout, breaking my foot, fighting against something that you love. It’s been hard,” he said. “Some of it has been quite painful, particularly from that foot injury onwards. “Coming back to where I am now and making the decision to go for LA, I think this is going to be the hardest climb I’ve ever faced and the hardest test. It’s really hard to see the summit because it’s so hard. I don’t think anyone understands.” What was perhaps most striking about that 59.65 was that it was nearly three seconds behind his world record – and slower even than he swam at the British trials in the spring. “I work a lot harder than a 59.6, really. It’s not a good time – we know that,” he said on Sunday. “When your world record is three seconds away, we’ve got to seriously ask what’s going wrong because that’s not me. “We need to look at it, interrogate it, look at the data, and ask whether it was an issue with race pace, fitness, or something else. I don’t think it was fitness, but there are a lot of components that make us swim, so we really have to analyse it.” He added: “I was fitter in April with less training, which doesn’t really make sense, to be honest. I guess that’s the learning point. Maybe I’m on a plan that I don’t fully understand, and maybe it’ll take another two years to find the right way.” On Saturday, Ramsay-Peaty also took aim at social media and traditional media too, which has become fixated with him and his pregnant wife, Holly – the daughter of the celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay – and his estrangement with his mother. “You don’t know who I am,” he said. “And people who comment, people who see the story because you read a headline, they’ve got to look themselves in the mirror. You can’t hurt me.” He added: “That hasn’t played a part in the sense of what I’ve experienced, because I’m still happy with that result in some sense, but it has to stop. How many athletes, how many people, have to go through this until the media learn their lesson? You have to learn and do better.”
chineseTitle: 亚当·拉姆齐-皮蒂制定了50米蛙泳黄金复兴的“作战计划”
chineseSummary: 英国人在英联邦运动会获得 100 米蛙泳铜牌后已经准备好反弹，他说：“过去 24 小时有点像旋风”
chineseContent: 亚当·拉姆齐-皮蒂从来都不是一个隐藏自己情绪的人。他自豪地将它们纹在袖子上，旁边是引人注目的巨大狮子和希腊海神波塞冬的纹身。在英联邦运动会上，这位 31 岁的选手在英联邦运动会 100m 蛙泳决赛中惨遭失利后，周日再次倾诉心声​​，并坚称他有一个“战斗计划”，希望能在周一的 50m 蛙泳决赛中赢得金牌。拉姆齐-皮蒂在排位赛中看起来确实更加顺利，从半决赛开始，成绩为 26.82 秒。然而，他与南非人迈克尔·霍利 (Michael Houlie) 相比仍有十分之几的差距，后者的最快成绩为 26.61。澳大利亚选手萨姆·威廉姆森希望在 100 米赛场上再添 50 米赛跑冠军，他的表现也不错，他以 26.79 的成绩赢得了半决赛。然而皮蒂表示，他对自己从周六的失利中恢复过来感到满意。 “感觉好多了，”他说。 “过去的 24 小时有点像旋风，但我对此感到非常高兴。明天我们正处于一个伟大的轨道上。“对我来说，把任何事情从我的脑海中解放出来的最好方法就是把它写下来。当我写下什么是错的、什么是对的、什么样的改变？什么是不能改变的？然后我就有了一个作战计划。”他补充道：“人们忘记了我已经两年没有这样做了。甚至我都忘记了这一点。所以当你经历预赛、半决赛和决赛时，如果你不习惯的话，那会很困难。所以我认为这种观点是一件好事。”在皮蒂辉煌的职业生涯中，他曾 32 次登上全球锦标赛领奖台。然而，自 2022 年伯明翰英联邦运动会以来，他还没有获得过金牌。周六，这一纪录被延续，当时他在 100 米蛙泳比赛中仅以 59.65 的成绩获得铜牌，落后于以 59.3 的成绩获胜的威廉姆森和才华横溢的 18 岁选手菲利普·诺维 (Filip Nowi)。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
